Tariffs are paid for at the consumer level. A 25% tax on car imports into China means that Chinese consumers are paying an extra 25%, not US car manufacturers. Therefore, if the US imposes a 25% tax on cars imported from China, then US consumers will pay an extra 25% on those cars, not Chinese auto manufacturers. What this does though, is it makes cars imported from China less sellable in the US market, because now they cost a bunch more, and will subsequently have a harder time competing with US built cars. This raises the average price of cars sold in the US market, thus potentially increasing the cost of living of US consumers... unless car factories are moved to/built in the US to avoid the tariffs. But then the US can no longer take advantage of lower foreign car production costs, so we will still see the result of higher costs for US consumers.

The reason auto manufacturers set up factories in places like China, is to cut costs, and thus profit more, but also provide less expensive cars to US consumers, making those cars more competitive in the US auto market. They also set up factories in China to avoid Chinese tariffs so that they can market more competitively to the Chinese car market.
